ai.literal: Enmity which is called, that which lacks good quality (acc.), a person, even in a joke, is not of the nature of desiring.
ai.translation: The evil thing called enmity should not be desired by anyone, even in jest.
ai.modern: பகை என்று சொல்லப்படும் தீய பண்பினை ஒருவன் விளையாட்டிற்காகக் கூட விரும்புதல் கூடாது.
ai.explanation: The couplet warns against entertaining enmity under any circumstances. The word 'pakai' (enmity) is described as 'paṇpu ilataṉai', meaning that which is entirely devoid of any good quality. Because it is inherently destructive, the poet advises that a person ('oruvaṉ') should not desire it ('vēṇṭaṟpāṟṟu aṉṟu') even as a joke ('nakaiyēyum'). This emphasizes that hatred is dangerous even when taken lightly.

ai.literal: Bow plough ploughmen enmity even if incurring, do not incur word plough ploughmen enmity.
ai.translation: Even if you incur the enmity of those who plough with a bow, do not incur the enmity of those who plough with words.
ai.modern: வில்லை ஏராகக் கொண்டு போர் செய்யும் வீரர்களின் பகையை அடைந்தாலும் அடையலாம், ஆனால் சொற்களை ஏராகக் கொண்டு செயல்படும் அறிஞர்களின் பகையை ஒருபோதும் அடையக்கூடாது.
ai.explanation: The couplet uses a striking agricultural metaphor to compare warriors and wise counselors. Warriors are described as ploughmen whose plough is the bow, while scholars and strategists are ploughmen whose plough is the word. It advises that while surviving the physical hostility of armed foes might be possible, making enemies of those who wield words and intellect will lead to certain ruin.

ai.literal: Even more than madmen, a fool [is] being alone, many people's enmity he who takes.
ai.translation: A man who stands alone and makes enemies of many is a greater fool than a madman.
ai.modern: தான் ஒருவனாக இருந்து பலருடைய பகையைத் தேடிக்கொள்பவன், பைத்தியம் பிடித்தவர்களை விடப் பெரிய முட்டாள் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the extreme danger of fighting on multiple fronts without allies. The word 'தமியனாய்' emphasizes the vulnerability of being completely alone. To deliberately provoke the hostility of many people in such an isolated state is described as a foolishness that surpasses even clinical madness.

ai.literal: Enemy as friendship having taken who conducts, quality possessor's in greatness rests the world.
ai.translation: The world rests on the greatness of the noble man who has the character to turn even an enemy into a friend.
ai.modern: பகைவரையும் நண்பராக மாற்றி நடக்கும் நல்ல பண்பு உடையவனின் பெருமையில்தான் இந்த உலகம் நிலைத்திருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the supreme value of turning enmity into friendship. The word pagai refers to an enemy, while natpaa kondu means making them into a friend. The world itself endures because of the greatness of such noble people who possess this rare character. By transforming hostility into harmony, they provide stability to the world.

ai.literal: One's own ally is not if, enemy two if, oneself one person; as sweet ally let take of them one.
ai.translation: If you stand alone without allies and face two enemies, make one of them a friendly ally.
ai.modern: தனக்கு ஒரு துணையும் இல்லாத நிலையில் பகைவர்கள் இருவராக இருந்தால், தனியாக இருக்கும் ஒருவன் அந்த இருவரில் ஒருவனைத் தனக்கு இனிய துணையாக ஆக்கிக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on strategic diplomacy when facing overwhelming odds. If a leader is completely isolated and confronted by two separate enemies, fighting both simultaneously is disastrous. The wise course of action is to temporarily befriend one of the enemies, turning them into an ally to divide the opposition and survive.

ai.literal: Even if trusted, even if left untrusted, at the time of ruin, without trusting, without alienating, let one leave (them).
ai.translation: Whether you have trusted someone before or not, in times of crisis, simply leave them be—neither placing trust in them nor openly alienating them.
ai.modern: ஒருவரை முன்பு நம்பியிருந்தாலும் அல்லது நம்பாமல் விட்டிருந்தாலும், நமக்கு ஒரு கேடு வரும் காலத்தில் அவரை மேலும் நம்பாமலும், அதே சமயம் பகைவராகப் பிரிக்காமலும் அப்படியே விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to handle people of uncertain loyalty during a crisis. The phrase 'தேறினும் தேறா விடினும்' covers all past relationships, meaning whether one had trusted them or not. In times of ruin ('அழிவின்கண்'), the safest course is 'விடல்', which means to simply leave them alone. One must do this 'தேறான்' (without placing new trust in them) and 'பகாஅன்' (without pushing them away to join the enemy).

ai.literal: Do not express pain, that which pained, to those who do not know; do not display weakness enemies in the presence of.
ai.translation: Do not express your pain to those who cannot understand it. Do not display your weakness in the presence of your enemies.
ai.modern: உங்கள் துன்பத்தை அதனைப் புரிந்து கொள்ளாதவர்களிடம் சொல்லாதீர்கள். உங்கள் பலவீனத்தை பகைவர்களிடத்தில் வெளிப்படுத்தாதீர்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet advises caution in revealing one's vulnerabilities to the wrong people. It warns against sharing grief with those who lack the empathy to understand it, as it brings no comfort. Similarly, it counsels against showing any sign of weakness to enemies, as they will exploit it to their advantage. The parallel commands 'நோவற்க' (do not express pain) and 'மேவற்க' (do not display) emphasize guarding one's inner state.

ai.literal: Nature having known, oneself having made, oneself if protecting, will perish among enemies arisen pride.
ai.translation: If one understands the nature of things, strengthens oneself, and guards oneself well, the pride that has arisen in one's enemies will perish.
ai.modern: சூழ்நிலைகளின் தன்மையை அறிந்து, தன்னை வலிமைப்படுத்திக் கொண்டு, தன்னைத் தற்காத்துக் கொண்டால், பகைவர்களிடம் உண்டான செருக்கு அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to defeat the arrogance of foes through careful preparation. The word 'வகை' (nature or categories) refers to understanding the various aspects of strength and weakness in a given conflict. 'தற்செய்து' means building up one's own power and resources, while 'தற்காப்ப' emphasizes the need for vigilant self-defense. When one is fully prepared and protected, the 'செருக்கு' (pride or overconfidence) that has arisen in the enemies will naturally 'மாயும்' (perish), as they realize their opponent cannot be easily defeated.

ai.literal: While tender thorn-tree let one destroy; of those who weed out hand it will hurt hardened at the time.
ai.translation: Cut down a thorny tree while it is still young and tender. If you wait until its trunk has hardened, it will injure the hands of those who try to chop it.
ai.modern: முள்மரத்தை அது இளமையாக இருக்கும்போதே வெட்டிவிட வேண்டும். அது முதிர்ந்து வயிரம் பாய்ந்த பிறகு வெட்ட நினைத்தால், வெட்டுபவரின் கையையே அது காயப்படுத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the vivid metaphor of a thorny tree to explain how to handle enemies. A thorny sapling is easy to uproot, but a mature one will injure the person trying to cut it down. Similarly, a foe's power should be dismantled while it is still weak and developing. If left to grow strong and entrenched, the enemy will cause great harm to anyone who attempts to defeat them later.

ai.literal: To breathe they exist they are not surely of those who are angry the pride those who cannot destroy.
ai.translation: Those who cannot destroy the pride of their foes are surely not alive, even if they breathe.
ai.modern: பகைவரின் செருக்கை அழிக்க முடியாதவர்கள் மூச்சு விட்டாலும் உயிருடன் இருப்பவர்கள் அல்லர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that merely breathing does not mean a person is truly alive. If a leader cannot crush the arrogance of their enemies, their existence is meaningless. The word cemmal here denotes the haughty pride of the foes, and manra emphasizes the absolute certainty of their lifeless state in a figurative sense.
